verdictInOneSentence: Every claim v7 was commissioned to make is true and independently reproduced -- the exhaustive ordering fact, the scoping derivation, the 1-live/0-after count, digestsMoved 0, and all four disclaimers -- but the value v7 asserts into the leaf it repaired re-publishes a falsified verification-status sentence ('no reviewer has verified either') one sentence away from its repair, which is the exact defect class v7 exists to remove, and this lineage's own precedent (B-EIR5-01) scores that class as blocking.

blockers.title: v7's asserted value re-carries 'no reviewer has verified either' -- a verification-status claim falsified by the v5 independent review, in the very leaf v7 rewrote
blockers.theSentence: That is the SECOND reproduction ever; v1's was the first and no reviewer has verified either.
blockers.whyFalse: evidence-identity-recipes.v5.review-independent.json (sha256 2152f8a68b6af6866a001abad318726ba75451df902e6b75b3b76a1a95735e69, dated 2026-08-12, the review that MINTED B-EIR5-01/B-EIR5-02) verified exactly this reproduction: its suite table carries 'evaluationProofBundleCasRef, assertions: 2 ... sha256:cc27c2be... reproduced from the EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS bundle by my own canonical-JSON encoder written from canonical-json-profile.v1 CJ-R01..R09, and independently by json.dumps(sort_keys,compact,ASCII); the two agree byte-for-byte. THIRD reproduction on record, failures: 0', and its claim table records 'second-ever reproduction of evaluationProofBundleCasRef cc27c2be...' -> 'verified: YES, AND MINE IS THE THIRD' at 9810 canonical bytes. A reviewer has therefore verified BOTH reproductions the sentence denies. The falsifying document is not obscure: v7's own predecessor cites it at v6#reviewBeingAnswered as the 275-assertion review.
blockers.whyThisIsNotProtectedHistory: The derivation rule's 'every set carries its exact prior value' governs the audit field 'from'; the 'value' field is what the successor ASSERTS, dated 2026-08-13, and v7 demonstrably edited other sentences inside this same leaf. Candidate bytes are repairable; nothing in section 7.2/7.6 protects them. The sentence is present-perfect and unscoped -- freeze section 7.2.2.1(a) item 4 requires such a self-measurement to be recomputed as a fixed point or scoped explicitly ('as of v5's authoring'); it is neither.
blockers.whyBlockerGrade: Three reasons. (1) Precedent inside this exact lineage: B-EIR5-01 -- a stale census sentence in prose -- was blocker-grade in the v5 review, and this is the same class. (2) It is the same MODE v7 was authored to repair: freeze section 7.2.2's rule 'a caveat is a measurement' and its finding that a false understatement of assurance 'buys the reader's trust with the appearance of candour' apply verbatim -- a reader deciding whether to trust cc27c2be is told it is unreviewed when it has been independently reproduced twice over by a reviewer (and a fourth time by this review). (3) v7's own thesis is that repairs must key on the defect class, not the instruction's symptom; it left a same-class false sentence standing in the leaf it rewrote.
blockers.theRepair: One sentence in a v8: either strike '; v1's was the first and no reviewer has verified either', or anchor it -- e.g. 'v1's was the first; as of v5's authoring no reviewer had verified either, and the v5 independent review has since reproduced the value by two independent routes as the third reproduction on record.' No digest, recipe or other leaf is touched.

advisories.title: The published vacuity predicate is narrower than the class it names -- variant spellings evade it
advisories.measured: The second alternation requires the literal spacing 'scalar value' and the connective from|versus|vs; the v6-corrected leaves' sentence 'scalar-value order and UTF-8-byte order are the SAME total order' fails to match only by HYPHENATION and connective choice, and the first alternation's [^.]{0,80} sentence segmentation is defeated by this corpus's habitual ' -- ' prose and by any future carrier spelled with 'code point', a hyphen, or a word-numeral. On the measured corpus this has no consequence -- my own broader predicates (co-occurrence of scalar/code-point vocabulary with UTF-8 within a leaf, BMP-clause in either spelling, distinguish/discriminate near order/sort, byte/code-unit order vocabulary) plus sentence-level reading of all 12 candidate leaves found no site the published predicate misses -- but the lineage's own history (the variant-spelling carrier in the v1 review, freeze 7.2.2.1(a) item 2) is exactly this instrument-fragility class biting. A successor predicate should tolerate hyphenation and name its spelling assumptions.
advisories.alsoNote: v7's stated reason the two v6-repaired leaves no longer match ('their corrected text names UTF-16 code units') is true of the caveat sentence proper, but the asymmetry signature is more fragile than stated: those leaves still pair scalar-value with UTF-8 vocabulary in their correction sentences and escape the predicate only via the hyphenation above.

rfc8785PrimarySourceConfirmation.status: CONFIRMED -- RFC 8785 JCS sorts object property names by UTF-16 code units
rfc8785PrimarySourceConfirmation.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.txt fetched during this review; fetched text sha256 63d52294eb0e3f0014174288186d388b4ddbf2c67d1ce8af1d9726eb0c3ab240
rfc8785PrimarySourceConfirmation.verbatim: Section 3.2.3: 'Property name strings to be sorted are formatted as arrays of UTF-16 [UNICODE] code units. The sorting is based on pure value comparisons, where code units are treated as unsigned integers, independent of locale settings.' The rationale paragraph adds that conversion from UTF-8 or UTF-32 to UTF-16 is required before sorting for systems using other representations.
rfc8785PrimarySourceConfirmation.theRFCsOwnTestVectorExecuted: The RFC's seven-key sorting vector was executed under all three orders: UTF-16 code-unit order reproduces the RFC's expected output EXACTLY; scalar order (== UTF-8 byte order, confirmed equal) does NOT -- it swaps the last two rows, emitting U+FB33 (Hebrew Letter Dalet With Dagesh) before U+1F600 (Emoji: Grinning Face), because 0xFB33 < 0x1F600 while UTF-16 compares 0xFB33 > 0xD83D. The RFC states this explicitly: sorting in UTF-8 or UTF-32 'would differ and thus be incompatible with this specification.'
rfc8785PrimarySourceConfirmation.consequence: The corpus's load-bearing assertion is TRUE as written everywhere it appears, so the exposure argument against applied delivery.v4 STANDS: delivery.v2#releaseManifestSchema.canonicalization (cited by delivery.v4 at DUD-V4-5) is sha256 over UTF8('opensip.release-manifest.v1\u0000') || JCS(manifest), JCS orders keys by UTF-16 code units, and UR-1's scalar/UTF-8 witnesses therefore genuinely conflict with it above the BMP. The settling vector in UR-1 is correct. Closing UR-1 itself remains the owning surface's act under section 6 law 19; this review only supplies the primary-source confirmation the sweep.v2 reviewer asked for.
